nodes.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a word $w$ over $\alpha$, the acceptance test is the Boolean that is true exactly when the state reached by running $D$ on $w$ from its start state is in the list of accepting states of $D$.
nodes.title: Acceptance test for encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $\alpha$ with a finite state set $\sigma$ with decidable equality, and let $n \ge |\sigma|$. For every state $p$ of the accessible part of $M$ found with $n$ rounds, some word $w$ leads the accessible part from its start state to $p$.
nodes.title: Every state of the accessible part is reached

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $\alpha$ with a finite state set $\sigma$ with decidable equality, and let $n \ge |\sigma|$. The accessible part of $M$ found with $n$ rounds is the DFA over $\alpha$ whose states are the states found by the reachability search from the empty set with at most $n$ rounds, whose start state is the start state of $M$, whose transition function is that of $M$ restricted to these…
nodes.title: Accessible part of a DFA, by a bounded search

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $\alpha$ with a finite state set $\sigma$ with decidable equality. The accessible part of $M$ is its accessible part found by the reachability search with $|\sigma|$ rounds: the DFA over $\alpha$ whose states are the states found by the reachability search from the empty set with at most $|\sigma|$ rounds (exactly the states that some word leads to from the start state of…
nodes.title: Accessible part of a DFA

nodes.summary: Let $D$ and $E$ be encoded DFAs over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality. The equivalence test of $D$ and $E$ is the Boolean that is true exactly when, for every entry $p$ of the list of reachable pairs of states of $D$ and $E$, writing $p = \langle s, t \rangle$ with Mathlib's pairing function, $s$ is in the accepting list of $D$ if and only if $t$ is in the accepting list of $E$.
nodes.title: Equivalence test for encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be DFAs over the same finite alphabet, with finite state sets with decidable equality and decidable sets of accepting states. The equivalence test of $M$ and $N$ returns true if and only if $M$ and $N$ accept the same language.
nodes.title: Correctness of the equivalence test for DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $M$ and $N$ be DFAs over the same finite alphabet, with finite state sets with decidable equality and decidable sets of accepting states. Their symmetric difference is the product DFA on pairs of states that starts at the pair of start states, moves on a letter by moving both components, and accepts a pair $(p, q)$ when exactly one of the statements "$M$ accepts $p$" and "$N$ accepts $q$" holds. The equivalence…
nodes.title: Equivalence test for DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, and let $N$ be the length of its list of states. For every natural number $n$ and every word $w$ of length $n$ in the language of $D$ with $N \le n$, the language of $D$ contains a word $v$ whose length $|v|$ satisfies $N \le |v| < 2N$.
nodes.title: Accepted words of length between the number of listed states and twice it

nodes.summary: For every encoded DFA $D$ over a finite alphabet, the infiniteness test returns true on $D$ if and only if the language of $D$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Correctness of the infiniteness test for encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA over a finite alphabet and let $N$ be the length of its list of states. The infiniteness test is the Boolean that is true exactly when the language of $D$ contains a word $w$ with $N \le |w| < 2N$; it checks every word of each length $N + i$ with $0 \le i < N$.
nodes.title: Infiniteness test for encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA and let $N$ be the length of the list of states of $D$. If $D$ accepts a word of length at least $N$, then the language of $D$ is infinite.
nodes.title: A long accepted word makes the language of an encoded DFA infinite

nodes.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, the emptiness test is the Boolean that is true exactly when no entry of the list of reachable states of $D$ is in the accepting list of $D$.
nodes.title: Emptiness test for encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. The emptiness test applied to $M$ returns true if and only if the language accepted by $M$ is empty.
nodes.title: The emptiness test decides emptiness of DFAs

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the emptiness test returns true exactly when none of the reachable states of $M$ is an accepting state.
nodes.title: Emptiness test for DFAs

nodes.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, the universality test is the Boolean that is true exactly when every entry of the list of reachable states of $D$ is in the accepting list of $D$.
nodes.title: Universality test for encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. The universality test applied to $M$ returns true if and only if $M$ accepts every word over the alphabet.
nodes.title: The universality test decides universality of DFAs

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the universality test applied to $M$ is the emptiness test applied to the complement of $M$: the DFA with the same states, start state and transitions whose accepting states are the states that $M$ does not accept.
nodes.title: Universality test for DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $s_0 \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{next}$ assign to every natural number a list of natural numbers, its successors, and let $B$ be a list of natural numbers that contains $s_0$ and is closed under successors: whenever $s$ is in $B$ and $t$ is a successor of $s$, then $t$ is in $B$. Then a natural number $t$ is in the list computed by the reachability search from $s_0$ through $\mathrm{next}$ within $B$ if and…
nodes.title: Correctness of the bounded reachability search

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. A state $s$ of $M$ is in the set of reachable states of $M$ if and only if there is a word $w$ such that running $M$ on $w$ from its start state ends in $s$.
nodes.title: A state is reachable exactly when some word leads to it

nodes.summary: Let $D$ and $E$ be encoded DFAs over the same alphabet, and let $p \in \mathbb{N}$ code the pair of states $(s, t)$ under the pairing bijection $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. The successors of $p$ form the list that has, for each letter $a$ in the letters of $D$ followed by the letters of $E$, the code of the pair made of the step of $D$ from $s$ on $a$ and the step of $E$ from $t$ on $a$.
nodes.title: Successors of a pair of states

nodes.summary: For encoded DFAs $D$ and $E$ over the same alphabet, code a pair $(s, t)$ of natural numbers by its image $\langle s, t \rangle \in \mathbb{N}$ under Mathlib's pairing function. The reachable pairs of $D$ and $E$ form the list returned by the bounded reachability search on lists of states started at $\langle s_D, s_E \rangle$, where $s_D$ and $s_E$ are the start states of $D$ and $E$, kept inside the list of coded…
nodes.title: Reachable pairs of states of two encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: For encoded DFAs $D$ and $E$ over the same alphabet, code a pair $(s, t)$ of natural numbers by its image $\langle s, t \rangle \in \mathbb{N}$ under Mathlib's pairing function. This is the list of the numbers $\langle s, t \rangle$ with $s$ running over the states of $D$ in their listed order and, for each $s$, $t$ running over the states of $E$ in their listed order.
nodes.title: Coded pairs of states of two encoded DFAs

nodes.summary: Let $s_0 \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{next}$ assign to each $s \in \mathbb{N}$ a list $\mathrm{next}(s)$ of natural numbers, and let $B$ be a list of natural numbers. One search round sends a list $R$ to the list obtained by writing $s_0$ followed, for each $s$ in $R$ in order, by $s$ and then the list $\mathrm{next}(s)$, keeping the entries that lie in $B$, and deleting every entry that occurs again later; its…
nodes.title: Bounded reachability search on lists of states

nodes.summary: Let $s_0 \in \mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{next}$ assign to each $s \in \mathbb{N}$ a list $\mathrm{next}(s)$ of natural numbers, and let $B$ and $R$ be lists of natural numbers. The round from $s_0$ with successors $\mathrm{next}$ kept inside $B$ sends the list $R$ of states found so far to the following list: write $s_0$ followed, for each $s$ in $R$ in order, by $s$ and then the list $\mathrm{next}(s)$; keep the…
nodes.title: One round of the list reachability search

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet $\alpha$. The round sends a finite set $S$ of states of $M$ to the set consisting of the start state of $M$ and of every state that the transition function of $M$ takes some $s \in S$ to on some letter $a \in \alpha$.
nodes.title: One round of the DFA reachability search

nodes.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$ over an alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality, the reachable states of $D$ form the list returned by the bounded reachability search on lists of states started at the start state of $D$, kept inside the states of $D$, in which the successors of a state $s$ are the states that the transition function of $D$ takes $s$ to on the letters of $D$, in the order of the letters.
nodes.title: Reachable states of an encoded DFA

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet with finitely many states. For every natural number $n$ at least the number of states of $M$, the early-stopping reachability search for $M$ from the empty set with at most $n$ rounds returns the set of reachable states of $M$.
nodes.title: The early-stopping search finds exactly the reachable states

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet whose set of states has decidable equality. For a natural number $n$ and a finite set $S$ of states of $M$, the reachability search from $S$ with at most $n$ rounds returns $S$ when $n = 0$. When $n = k + 1$, it returns $S$ if one round of the reachability search for $M$ sends $S$ to $S$ itself, and otherwise it returns the search from the image of $S$ under that round with…
nodes.title: Early-stopping DFA reachability search

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet whose set of states $\sigma$ is finite and has decidable equality. The reachable states of $M$ form the finite set obtained from the empty set by applying one round of the DFA reachability search for $M$ exactly $|\sigma|$ times, where $|\sigma|$ is the number of states of $M$.
nodes.title: Reachable states of a DFA

nodes.summary: For a DFA $M$ over a finite alphabet with finitely many states, the start state of $M$ belongs to the reachable states of $M$.
nodes.title: The start state is reachable

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a DFA over a finite alphabet whose set of states is finite and has decidable equality. If a state $s$ of $M$ is reachable from the start state, then for every letter $a$ the state to which $M$ moves from $s$ on $a$ is also reachable from the start state.
nodes.title: Reachable states are closed under transitions

nodes.summary: For DFAs $M$ and $N$ over the same alphabet, with sets of states $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$, this is the product DFA with set of states $\sigma \times \sigma'$ whose start state is the pair of the start states of $M$ and $N$, whose transition takes $(p, q)$ on a letter $a$ to the pair of the state to which $M$ moves from $p$ on $a$ and the state to which $N$ moves from $q$ on $a$, and whose accepting states are the…
nodes.title: Symmetric difference of two DFAs

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ that its language is the set of all words over $\alpha$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $\mathrm{ALL}_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.
nodes.title: Universality of DFAs is decidable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ that its language is empty is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $E_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.
nodes.title: Emptiness of DFAs is decidable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair of encoded DFAs over $\alpha$ that their languages are equal is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $\mathrm{EQ}_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.
nodes.title: Equivalence of DFAs is decidable

nodes.summary: For every finite alphabet $\alpha$, given with an enumeration of its letters, decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of an encoded DFA over $\alpha$ that its language is infinite is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $\mathrm{INFINITE}_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.
nodes.title: Infiniteness of DFAs is decidable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $\alpha$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(D, w)$ of an encoded DFA $D$ over $\alpha$ and a word $w$ over $\alpha$ that $w$ belongs to the language of $D$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine. This is the problem $A_{\mathrm{DFA}}$.
nodes.title: Acceptance for DFAs is decidable

nodes.summary: For an encoded DFA $D$, this is the DFA whose set of states is the finite set of states of $D$ (its start state and the targets of its listed transitions), whose start state is the start state of $D$, whose transition function is that of $D$ restricted to these states, and whose accepting states are those in the accepting list of $D$.
nodes.title: An encoded DFA on its listed states

nodes.summary: For a finite alphabet $\alpha$ given with an enumeration of its letters and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the list of the words of length $n$ over $\alpha$: starting from the list whose only entry is the empty word, it replaces $n$ times each word $w$ of the current list by the words $a w$ for the letters $a$ of $\alpha$, in their enumeration order.
nodes.title: Words of a given length

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
